name: Post-earnings-announcement drift on earnings surprise (long-only)
rule: Universe Nifty 500, price>50. On each quarterly result compute UE=(EPS_q-EPS_q4)/close[day-2]. Rank against previous quarter's cross-sectional quartile breakpoints. If top quartile, buy at open of day+2 (day0 = first session able to react). Hold 63 trading days or until next result. Equal weight, max 6 names, oldest replaced. Optional 15% stop.
reported_performance: India 2008-2014 (18,269 announcements): market-adjusted return days +2..+64 was +0.7% for top UE quartile, -6.6% for bottom; spread 7.3%. BSE 2001-2006 (Sen 2009): quintile spread 10.05% per quarter. India 2014-2018 (100 NSE firms): no exploitable drift.
feasibility_reason: Fully implementable long-only with small positions, but the Indian long leg earned under 1% a quarter over the index, less than the 0.5% round-trip cost plus tax; most of the spread is on the unshortable side.

name: Earnings-announcement-return (EAR) drift, alone or intersected with SUE
rule: Universe Nifty 500, price>50. EAR = stock return minus Nifty 500 return over sessions day-1..day+1 around the result. Quintile breakpoints from previous quarter. Long if EAR in top quintile (if require_sue: also SUE in top quintile). Buy at open of day+2, hold 60 trading days, equal weight, max 6 positions.
reported_performance: US 1987-2004 (Brandt et al. via Quantpedia): EAR long-short 7.55%/yr abnormal; EAR-and-SUE intersection +2.97% long vs -0.58% short per 60 days (about 15%/yr); max drawdown -11.2%; weaker but present in 1,000 largest firms.
feasibility_reason: Needs only prices and result dates and trades long-only, but no Indian test exists and the entry is after a gap; edge must exceed about 0.5% costs per trade.

name: Price-and-volume shock drift (earnings-gap proxy from daily bars)
rule: Universe Nifty 500, price>50. Signal day t: open >= 1.04*prev close, close in top 30% of day range, volume >= 3x 50-day average, close > 200-day SMA, Nifty 500 > its 200-day SMA. Buy open t+1. Exit after 20 trading days or on close below low of day t. Max 5 positions, equal weight.
reported_performance: No sampled, cost-adjusted result found (searched Nov 2026); practitioner descriptions only. Underlying drift evidence is the US EAR result for 1987-2004.
feasibility_reason: Long-only, liquid universe, 5 positions of about Rs 30,000; unproven and included because it is testable from daily OHLCV alone.

name: Triple-sorted momentum: price, earnings surprise, revenue surprise
rule: Universe Nifty 500. Monthly, rank on (a) prior 6-month return, (b) latest earnings surprise, (c) latest revenue surprise (year-on-year seasonal change, standardised). Long stocks in top tercile on all three; hold 6 months in overlapping monthly cohorts; equal weight; max 10 names. Breakpoints not given in abstract: test terciles and quintiles.
reported_performance: BSE 500 (493 firms), Jan 2002-Jun 2010 (Sehgal and Jain 2015): triple-sorted portfolio 2.28% per month, gross; earnings momentum most profitable long-short; reversal after holding period.
feasibility_reason: Long-only monthly rotation of up to 10 small positions is workable; sample is old and gross, turnover costs 2-4% a year.

name: Negative earnings surprise: exit overlay or futures short
rule: After a result with UE in bottom quartile (previous-quarter breakpoints) or 3-day announcement return in bottom quintile: overlay mode sells any holding and blocks buys for 63 trading days; short mode sells near-month stock future at open of day+2, holds 63 trading days with one roll, stop +12%.
instruments: Overlay on cash holdings; single-stock futures for the short
reported_performance: India 2008-2014: bottom UE quartile -6.6% market-adjusted over days +2..+64; second quartile -2.0%.
feasibility_reason: Overlay is free and usable; the short needs one stock-futures lot whose margin can exceed the whole account, so the profitable leg is not accessible.

name: Holding through the results announcement (announcement premium)
rule: Buy at close two sessions before a scheduled results date; sell at close one session after. Optional filter: previous quarter's UE in top quartile. Max 5 concurrent positions.
reported_performance: India 2008-2014 (18,269 announcements): mean 3-day market-adjusted return -0.5%, median -0.7%, about 57% negative.
feasibility_reason: Mechanically easy, but the measured expectation is negative before 0.5% costs; listed so a backtest can close the idea.

name: Analyst BUY recommendation drift
rule: Universe Nifty 100. Event: new BUY or upgrade to BUY from a broker. Buy next open, hold 20 trading days, equal weight, max 5 positions, at most one entry per stock per 20 days. Ignore SELL calls.
reported_performance: Nifty 50 firms 2012-2018 (Moulya and Mallikarjunappa): no announcement-day reaction, delayed drift after BUY calls; magnitude not extracted. IIMB study: target hits driven by market moves, not analyst insight.
feasibility_reason: Capital is sufficient; the obstacle is a timestamped recommendations feed and a signal that fires constantly because most calls are BUY.

name: Promoter and insider open-market buying (PIT disclosures)
rule: Universe NSE stocks, market cap 500-20,000 crore, turnover>2 crore/day. Event: PIT Reg 7 disclosure, category promoter/director/KMP, mode market purchase, value >= 1 crore. Prefer >=2 insiders within 30 days and negative prior 3-month return. Buy next open after exchange disclosure. Hold 90 trading days. Max 6 positions, equal weight, 20% stop.
reported_performance: India 2008-2014 (about 32,000 insider trade days): buys -0.20% market-adjusted at 1 month; buy-minus-sell spread 1.53% at 3 months and 8.22% at 1 year, mostly from sells. 2026 study: +6.67% over 90 days after purchases (unverified: snippet only).
feasibility_reason: Slow long-only signal, free NSE data, positions of Rs 25,000 are fine; expect modest edge and filter out non-market acquisitions.

name: Red-flag exclusion overlay: insider selling, pledge increase, rating downgrade
rule: Exclude a stock from all long universes: 250 trading days after net insider/promoter market sales > 1 crore within 30 days; while promoter pledge > 25% of promoter holding or after a rise of >= 5 points quarter on quarter; 60 trading days after a long-term rating downgrade by CRISIL/ICRA/CARE. Ignore upgrades.
reported_performance: Insider sells precede declines (8.22% 1-year buy-sell spread, 2008-2014). Pledging raises crash risk (257 BSE 500 firms, 2011-2020). Downgrades: negative returns mostly before the announcement (top 100 NSE firms 2009-2019; banks study 2023).
feasibility_reason: No capital or trading cost; needs insider, pledge and rating feeds.

name: Following bulk-deal buyers
rule: Event: NSE bulk-deal file shows a client buying >0.5% of equity in a stock with no bulk sell that day (Only Buy). Buy at next open; sell at close after 5 trading days. Price>20, turnover>2 crore.
reported_performance: NSE 2010-2019 (Rajvanshi; 1,804 single-investor Only-Buy deals): +3.46% on deal day, +0.71% day +1, then negative each day +2..+7 (about -1.1%); partial-buy deals about -2.0% over days +2..+7.
feasibility_reason: Easy to trade, but the disclosure arrives after the move and the following drift is negative before costs.

name: Rebound after bulk-deal selling
rule: Event: Only Sell bulk deal (client sells >0.5% of equity, no bulk buy that day) and stock closed down on deal day. Price>20, turnover>2 crore. Buy next open; sell at close after 5 trading days; 5% stop.
reported_performance: NSE 2010-2019: single-investor Only-Sell deals (N=2,831) -0.87% on deal day then about +1.0% cumulative over days +1..+7; multi-investor (N=77) +1.63% and +1.51% on days +1 and +2.
feasibility_reason: About 1.0% gross is consumed by 0.5% round-trip cost and the opening gap; only worth testing on larger down-moves.

name: Block-deal purchases by long-term institutions or insiders
rule: Event: block-window purchase where buyer is a mutual fund, insurer, pension/sovereign fund or promoter entity and seller is not a promoter. Buy next open; hold 3 trading days (test 20). Max 3 positions.
instruments: NSE cash equities (large and mid cap)
reported_performance: India 2005-2015 (2,547 buy-side block trades): 3-day Fama-French-adjusted return positive for purchases by pressure-resistant institutions and insiders, stronger after 2010; magnitude not legible in extract.
feasibility_reason: Liquid names and small positions are fine, but the window is centred on the trade so the public follower gets less; costs 0.5% on a 3-day hold.

name: Index inclusion: announcement to effective date (Nifty 50, Next 50, MSCI India)
rule: Event: official addition announcement (NSE Indices press release after hours; MSCI about 03:30 IST). Buy at open of first session after announcement unless gap > 5%. Sell at close of last session before effective date (ED-1). Never hold past ED-1. 30% of capital per event, max 3 concurrent.
reported_performance: MSCI, 56 markets 2006-2023: long adds/short deletes from announcement close to ED-1 close about 5.4% (6.1% Asia-Pacific) after lending fees. Nifty 1996-2003: no announcement effect, +1.47% effective day, reversed by day 9. Nifty 2000-2016: inclusion gains reverse within 60 days.
feasibility_reason: Liquid stocks, long-only, few events (1-4 Nifty 50 and roughly 15-30 MSCI India additions a year); Indian evidence is mixed and the published figure includes a short leg.

name: Index deletion rebound
rule: Event: stock removed from Nifty 50 or MSCI India for size/liquidity reasons (skip mergers, delistings, suspensions, regulatory removals). Buy at close of last session before effective date. Hold 120 trading days. 25% of capital per name, 20% stop. Optional filter: trailing 12-month profit positive.
reported_performance: Nifty 50 2000-2016: excluded stocks +4% to +7% abnormal over 60-240 days. MSCI India 2015-2019: +16% one year after exclusion vs +8% after inclusion. Nifty 50 last five years to 2026: 7 of 10 deletions up after 6 months, 9 of 10 after a year.
feasibility_reason: Long-only, liquid, very low turnover; only 2-4 Nifty 50 events a year and small samples.

name: Pre-positioning in predicted Nifty 50 additions
rule: On first trading day after cut-off (1 Feb, 1 Aug): candidates = Nifty 100 members in F&O, not in Nifty 50, with 6-month average free-float market cap >= 1.5x that of the smallest Nifty 50 constituent, 100% trading frequency, impact cost <= 0.50%. Buy top-ranked candidate; sell at close on announcement day. 25% of capital, max 2 names.
reported_performance: No tested Indian result. Broker claim of 8-15% excess return in the 20 days before MSCI announcements (unverified: snippet only). US: pre-announcement run-ups became somewhat stronger as the announcement effect vanished (1980-2020).
feasibility_reason: Capital is enough for one or two liquid names, but it needs free-float data, yields one or two trades a year and overlaps with plain momentum.

name: F&O list inclusion and exclusion
rule: Inclusion date = first day a symbol appears in the F&O bhavcopy (or circular date if available). Buy cash stock at open after the circular; sell at close of first F&O trading day. Exclusion flag = symbol has no contract for newest expiry month while others do: exit and block buys.
reported_performance: India 2001-2020 event study: positive reaction on inclusion, negative on exclusion (unverified: snippet only). Dec 2021/Jan 2022 additions: 6-month post-inclusion returns mostly negative (e.g. -27%, -30%, -18%, -15%; two clear gainers).
feasibility_reason: Tradable long-only in liquid names; events are lumpy and evidence of any sustained gain is absent.

name: Tender-offer buyback through the small-shareholder quota
rule: Event: tender buyback at price Pb. Estimate acceptance AR = min(1, 0.15*buyback_shares/small_holder_shares/participation). Enter if Pb/P0-1 >= 0.10 and AR*(Pb/P0-1) >= 0.03. Buy N = floor(min(0.6*capital, 190000)/P0) shares by record date minus 1 session, keeping N*record close <= 200000. Tender all. Sell returned shares at open after credit, or stop at P0-(AR/(1-AR))*(Pb-P0).
instruments: NSE cash equities plus broker tender window
reported_performance: Cases: HCL Tech 2017 acceptance 148/220, about 10% in 3 months; TCS 2022 acceptance about 25% at 12-15% premium; L&T 2023 expected 25-30% at 8.5% premium; Infosys 2025 entitlement 2:11. Acceptance has fallen since 2016. Viable again after tax change of 1 Apr 2026.
feasibility_reason: The Rs 2 lakh small-shareholder cap matches the account size; risks are low acceptance, post-buyback price drop on a concentrated position, tax-rule changes, and tendering that may not be automatable.

name: Buyback announcement drift (no tendering)
rule: Event: board intimation to consider buyback, or approval of a tender buyback with premium >= 10% and size >= 2% of equity. Buy next open. Sell at close two sessions before record date (or after 10 trading days if no record date yet). Max 3 positions.
reported_performance: India (IIMA working paper): significant positive abnormal returns around tender and open-market repurchase announcements; open-market repurchasers later underperform. 2006-2024 study: 5.9% pre-announcement run-up post-2015 attributed to leakage (unverified: snippet only).
feasibility_reason: Simple long-only trade, but much of the move precedes the public announcement and the remaining drift is unquantified against 0.5% costs.

name: Open-offer (takeover) tender arbitrage
rule: Event: open offer at price Po for X% of shares. Expected acceptance A = offer_shares / expected_tendered_public_shares. Enter if market price <= 0.95*Po and A >= 0.5. Tender all; sell leftovers at open after offer closes. Override: sell in market whenever price >= Po. Max 20% of capital.
instruments: NSE/BSE cash equities plus tender window
reported_performance: India 2015-2017 (31 large offers): higher abnormal returns in days 0..+30 than before. India 2007-2010 (187 offers): negative post-announcement returns. Since 2013, 133 offers, only a handful fully subscribed; United Spirits acceptance 55% vs 70% expected.
feasibility_reason: Partial acceptance leaves unhedged leftover shares; the futures hedge professionals use is out of reach; tax treatment of tendered shares in 2026 unconfirmed.

name: Voluntary delisting: reverse book-building or fixed-price offer
rule: Event: promoter delisting proposal. RBB mode: buy if price <= 1.15*floor; bid 1.4*floor in the book; if discovered price rejected and counter-offer fails, sell at market. Fixed-price mode: buy if price <= 0.96*fixed price and promoter plus committed holders can reach 90%. Stop 12% below entry. Max 20% of capital.
instruments: NSE/BSE cash equities plus tender window
reported_performance: No systematic study found. Law-firm notes (2024-2025): RBB prices at times more than double the floor; success needs 90%; fixed price must be >= 15% above floor; counter-offer allowed at >= 75% post-offer holding with >= 50% of public float tendered.
feasibility_reason: Binary outcomes, a handful of illiquid events a year, cannot be backtested from prices; position must stay small.

name: Share-swap merger arbitrage, long target
rule: Event: amalgamation scheme with swap ratio r (acquirer shares per target share). Spread = r*P_acquirer/P_target - 1. Buy target when spread >= 6% and record date expected within 6 months. Exit when spread < 1% or on record date. If both are in F&O and margin allows, short r units of acquirer futures. Max 25% of capital.
instruments: NSE cash equities; stock futures for hedge
reported_performance: Examples only: Harita Seating/Minda Industries 2019 spread 8.13% gross, 6.92% after tax, unhedgeable; HDFC/HDFC Bank 2022-2023 spread 1-3% over about 15 months (unverified: snippet only).
feasibility_reason: Without the acquirer short the position is just long the acquirer by proxy for months; the hedge needs a futures lot beyond this account.

name: Demerger announcement drift
rule: Event: board approves a demerger scheme. Buy parent at next open; sell at close after 5 trading days. Price>50, turnover>2 crore. Max 3 positions, equal weight. Variant: low-priced stocks only (below cross-sectional median price).
reported_performance: India 2003-2020 (221 BSE firms): +1.35% abnormal on day +1, 2.64% cumulative over days +1..+5; days -10..+10: 3.90% high-priced, 7.16% low-priced. India 2012-2014 (51 demergers): +1.74% on announcement.
feasibility_reason: Tradable, but 2.6% gross includes the opening gap and must cover 0.5% costs; a dozen or two events a year.

name: Newly listed demerged entity
rule: Event: demerged company lists. Wait for first session that does not close at the lower price band; buy next open. Hold 250 trading days; 25% stop. Skip if last reported annual profit is negative. Max 15% of capital per name.
reported_performance: No Indian sample study found. 2015 press review: about half of listed spin-offs gave negative returns with very wide dispersion (figures unverified: snippet only).
feasibility_reason: Small long-only positions are possible; few events, no price history and high dispersion make it hard to validate.

name: Rights-entitlement discount arbitrage
rule: During a rights issue: if P_share - (P_RE + issue_price) >= 0.03*P_share and share turnover > 2 crore, buy RE, apply for rights shares, sell shares at open on credit day. Abort if share price falls below issue_price*1.05 before application. Max 20% of capital.
instruments: Rights entitlements, NSE cash equities, rights application
reported_performance: No return study found. Process since 7 Apr 2025 completes in 23 working days. Rights/FPO issuers 2000-2014 lagged matched firms by 17% over 5 years.
feasibility_reason: Capital is enough, but RE liquidity is thin, there is no overnight hedge until allotment, and the application step is manual.

name: Equity-issuer avoidance: QIP, rights issue, FPO
rule: Exclude a stock from all long universes for 126 trading days after a QIP opens and 250 trading days after a rights issue or FPO closes.
reported_performance: 84 QIPs 2010-2016: average 3- and 6-month holding returns negative every year and below BSE 500. 177 rights/FPO issuers 2000-2014: 17% below matched firms over 5 years.
feasibility_reason: A filter with no capital requirement; needs an issuance calendar.

name: OFS retail-discount capture
rule: Event: exchange OFS with retail discount d. On retail day bid at cut-off for up to 30% of capital if (prev_close - floor*(1-d))/prev_close >= 0.04 and non-retail book >= 2x subscribed. Sell at open on the day shares are credited.
instruments: OFS bid then NSE cash sale
reported_performance: No return study found. 39 NSE OFS, Mar 2012-Jul 2023: significant price declines before PSU OFS announcements (floor-price leakage).
feasibility_reason: Affordable, but the stock often falls toward the floor on OFS day, there is no hedge, and bidding is unlikely to be available by API.

name: Mainboard IPO retail application with subscription filter
rule: Mainboard book-built IPOs only. On last day after 14:00 apply for one retail lot at cut-off if QIB subscription >= 20x and total >= 10x. Ignore grey-market premium unless negative (then skip). If allotted, sell at listing-day open, or hold with stop at issue price until close.
instruments: IPO application (UPI/ASBA), then NSE cash sale
holding_period: about one week blocked; under one day market exposure
reported_performance: SEBI study, 144 mainboard IPOs Apr 2021-Dec 2023: 75% listed positive, 26 gained over 50%. 2025 (108 IPOs): median listing gain 3.8% vs 15.2% in 2024; about 8% average in early 2026.
feasibility_reason: One lot is about Rs 15,000 and several can overlap; allotment odds are roughly 1 over the retail subscription multiple, so expected rupee gain per application is small; application automation unconfirmed.

name: Buying IPOs in the secondary market on or after listing day
rule: Listing date = first bhavcopy appearance (exclude demerger listings). Variant A: buy listing-day close, hold 60 trading days. Variant B: after >= 15 sessions buy first close above highest close since listing; stop = lowest low of last 10 sessions; exit on close below 50-day SMA or after 120 days. Max 4 positions.
reported_performance: 2025: only 41% of 108 mainboard IPOs above listing price at year-end. 377 IPOs 2005-2015: 36-month abnormal return -57.33%, about 10% beat the index. 2012-2025 study: average +20.29% at 1 year fading to +8.72% at 3 years (secondary reports).
feasibility_reason: Tradable with small positions; evidence for buy-and-hold from listing is negative and the breakout variant is untested.

name: Anchor lock-in expiry
rule: Unlock dates = allotment date + 30 and + 90 calendar days (allotment about 3 sessions before listing). Overlay: hold no recent IPO from 3 sessions before to 2 after the 30-day unlock. Contrarian: if first unlocked session closes down >= 5% on volume >= 3x 20-day average, buy that close, sell after 5 trading days.
reported_performance: SEBI staff study, 242 mainboard IPOs Apr 2022-Oct 2025: mean price impact in 30-day unlock window from about -0.4% (anchor exits <= 2.5%) to -3.5% (exits > 10%); 90-day window more muted; anchors exit 3.2% at T+30, 17.3% after T+90, 51% by T+365.
feasibility_reason: Overlay costs nothing; the contrarian leg is small, long-only and untested; no shorting possible in new listings.

name: Bonus and stock-split announcements
rule: Event: board approves bonus issue or forward split. Buy next open; sell at close after 10 trading days. Price>50, turnover>2 crore, max 3 positions. Variant: buy 5 sessions before ex-date, sell at ex-date close.
reported_performance: India 2010-2015 (23 forward splits): +1.61% abnormal around announcement day (significant), +1.28% on split day (not significant). Other Indian studies: positive bonus announcement effect, mixed for splits (unverified: snippet only).
feasibility_reason: A 1-2% effect concentrated on the announcement day cannot be captured after the fact and is about the size of costs.

name: Daily FII/DII flow as next-day index signal
rule: After close read provisional FII net cash-market figure. If FII net > 0 (variant: above its 20-day mean), hold Nifty ETF for the next session, else cash. Monthly variant: hold if prior month FII net > 0.
reported_performance: India, 4,402 trading days from 12 Nov 2007: next-day market up about 50% of the time whether FIIs bought or sold the day before; same-day 56%; monthly co-movement about 70% is contemporaneous; FIIs buy after up days 63% of the time.
feasibility_reason: Trivially tradable with an ETF, but the data show no lead from flows to returns and daily switching costs are pure drag.

name: Upper-circuit momentum
rule: Universe NSE EQ series with 5/10/20% band, price>20, 20-day median turnover>1 crore; exclude 2% band, BE/T2T, SME, ASM/GSM. Signal: close >= prev close*(1+band) - tick, volume >= 2x 20-day average, 10-day gain <= 40%. Buy next open only if open < that day's upper band. Exit first close not at upper band, or close below prior low, or 5 sessions. 10% of capital each.
instruments: NSE cash equities (small and micro cap)
reported_performance: No study or credible backtest found (searched Nov 2026). Exchange mechanics: at upper circuit buyers queue with no sellers, so new buys may not fill.
feasibility_reason: Capital is sufficient, but winning trades tend not to fill and losing ones can lock at lower circuit; naive backtests overstate results.
